lesson: SFPU mul_binary_tile (DST-DST) costs more than the acquire/commit/wait/release + CB_T_TMP reserve/pack/push/wait/pop roundtrip it saves. Bit-identical (PSNR ∞, diff10 black) but kernel ms regressed 99.95 → 100.69. Don't use SFPU DST-DST as a perf fusion. Next: try FPU binary_dest_reuse_tiles<ELWMUL, DEST_TO_SRCA> for same fusion.

Render daemon hung within cycle 1; no per-cycle timing line emitted. ORIGINAL HYPOTHESIS: per-channel D2 fuse (copy_tile + mul_unary_tile + binary_dest_reuse_tiles<ELWADD, DEST_TO_SRCA>) deadlocks via SFPU/FPU mixed chain through binary_dest_reuse_tiles. CORRECTION: after iter-009, discovered that the dev viewer's daemon holds /dev/tenstorrent/0 silently — concurrent dispatches just hang. The iter-008 hang may have been device contention, not a real kernel bug. Status: untested. Re-run only after killing all device-holding processes. Until proven, treat SFPU/FPU mixed chains across binary_dest_reuse_tiles as suspect (matches the M2 86c5ae2 deadlock pattern), but the iter-008 result alone is no longer conclusive evidence.

Collapsing 3 FPU mul_tiles (dx²/dy²/dx·dy) into one acquire regressed kernel ms 99.34 → 100.70 (+1.37%) while producing bit-identical output. Same negative result as iter-006: removing acquire cycles for FPU ops eliminates overlap between pack and the next stage's setup. The 3 muls run serially inside one acquire and pack waits at tile_regs_release. Three explicit acquires let pack overlap with the next setup. Lesson: don't fuse independent FPU ops into one acquire just to save acquire/commit/wait/release cycles — the pack/setup overlap is more valuable than the cycles saved.

Stacking two binary_dest_reuse<ELWADD, DEST_TO_SRCA> applications in one acquire (add_tiles + binary_dest_reuse on CB_Q) drops PSNR ~1 dB further than a single application. Combined with iter-007's and iter-010's ~1 dB drops each, hero went 40.40 → 39.69 and top 40.15 → 38.87 — both below the 40 dB kernel-algebra floor. AND kernel ms 97.77 → 97.90 (+0.13%, break-even within noise). DEST_TO_SRCA reload appears to truncate to bf16 between ops; pure pack/unpack roundtrips preserve precision better. Budget remaining binary_dest_reuse applications carefully — we can afford at most 1-2 more before the 35 dB hard floor. Pick big-acquire-savings fusions only.

Multi-slot fill_tile in one acquire deadlocks the kernel. Two variants tried: (A) pack_tile(3, CB_T_STATE) + pack_tile(3, CB_SAT_MASK) reusing same dst slot — hang. (B) 2-acquire form: fill_tile(0..3) for R/G/B/T then fill_tile(0) for SAT_MASK — also hang. Both blocked daemon in futex_wait_queue_me holding /dev/tenstorrent/0. No working multi-slot fill_tile precedent in tt-metal programming_examples or tests. fill_tile.h says idst is unconstrained, but in practice the SFPU fill pipeline appears to require single-slot use. For per-tile state init, stick with the original 5-acquire pattern OR use copy_tile from a pre-populated CB_CONST tile. Don't try multi-slot fill_tile again without a tt-metal reference example.

Removing binary_dest_reuse<ELWMUL, DEST_TO_SRCA>(CB_SAT_MASK) from iter-010's fused acquire deadlocks the kernel. Two attempts (one on dirty device, one with fresh JIT cache + verified clean device) both hung at cycle 1 within 5 min. The mul_tiles → binary_dest_reuse → pack triad is not freely reversible: pack_tile appears to depend on internal pipeline state established by binary_dest_reuse_tiles_init, even though it nominally reads from dst[0] which holds the mul_tiles result. Lesson: to recover PSNR headroom from iter-007/iter-010 fusions, the *whole triad* must be reverted to a 2-acquire form, not just the binary_dest_reuse half. Plan doc preserved in iter-013-drop-stage-e-sat-mask.md.

reject_reason: DEVICE_HANG: CB_SCALARS depth=4 with mixed singleton+pair batches drifts the CB write pointer; a pair starting at slot 3 wraps to [3,0] which are non-contiguous in L1, corrupting subsequent reads. Theoretical wrap-straddle rate ~25%, in practice device hangs within first few tiles.

PSNR floor violation: hero 33.59 dB, top 33.22 dB — both >1 dB below the 35 dB binning floor. Kernel speedup only 0.71% (23.98→23.81 ms) far too small to justify quality drop. LoFi (1 FPU pass/tile vs HiFi3's 3) is too aggressive for the alpha-blend's 8 FPU ops/Gaussian. Interesting: tile_structure_ratio actually IMPROVED (hero 16.7→10.7) suggesting LoFi noise is less tile-correlated than HiFi3 quantization — but PSNR magnitude loss dominates.
